name: previous_day_high_low_breakout_5s
author: adapted from claude_strategist
thesis: Previous day's high and low are the most-watched support/resistance levels by both retail and institutional traders. When price breaks these levels with conviction (volume + close beyond level), stop-loss triggers from the prior day's trapped traders create momentum. The inefficiency exists because PDH/PDL are anchoring points for human decision-making — behavioral finance research confirms that round levels and recent extremes attract disproportionate order clustering.
mechanism: Consolidation periods accumulate resting orders above resistance and below support. A breakout triggers these resting orders as stop-losses and breakout entries fire simultaneously. The resulting order flow imbalance overwhelms the resting liquidity, and market makers widen spreads in the breakout direction, accelerating the move.

conditions: dist_from_pdh > 5 AND dist_from_pdh < 30 (clean break, not overextended)

filters.expiry_filter: skip on expiry day, stock results day

weaknesses: False breakouts at PDH/PDL are extremely common — 50% win rate means half the time it fails
On inside days (today's range inside yesterday's), PDH/PDL may never be tested
If many stocks break PDH/PDL simultaneously, it's a macro-driven day and edge comes from market direction, not the level
prior_art: Previous Day High/Low breakout — Linda Raschke, Mark Fisher. Ancient setup.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
